newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH TOWN SURVIVES WATER ATTACK, FLOOD RECEDES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH TOWN SURVIVES WATER ATTACK, FLOOD RECEDES.

text.p: The Polish town of Slubice on the German border, where 15,000 people were evacuated as the River Odra threatened to swamp the area, survived the water's onslaught and floods receded in other regions on Monday.

"The flood situation is stabilising. Slubice has so far resisted the river, whose level has begun to slowly decline. But the fight to save the sodden dikes continues," crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes told Reuters.

The town, just accross the river from Frankfurt an der Oder, may still face a renewed threat of complete flooding when the second surge on the Odra, now some 200 km away from the town, reaches the area in several days, he said.

Pomes said that on the average the floods, which still affected nearly 2,000 sq km in southern and western Poland, were set to further decline as the weather forecast was for sunshine and only occasional showers in the next few days.
The authorites have ordred evacuation of several hundred people in the southeastern province of Przemysl, where the so far relatively calm San river threatened two municipalities.

The three-week-old floods, the worst in centuries, have left a death toll of 55 and with more than 40,000 people still displaced. Independent analysts have estimated the damages at up to 7.5 billion zlotys ($2.3 billion).

Many people have been returning home, finding debris, filth and dead livestock. The government has granted tax breaks, cheap credits and other aid for the affected areas, but many flood victims complain the relief action is chaotic.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz has ordered a meeting of the National Programme of Reconstruction and Modernisation Council for Monday to work out details of long-term relief and rebuilding operations. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
